The route needs a candidate that can change package-lock.json. CQ-R11e3a treats lockfiles as untrusted, but task-5ed445ca's plan assumed the admitted lockfile is protected.

implementationPlan.description:
Add DA9 and DA10 at the END of scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs, after KI8. They need NPM_CLI, NO_NPM, INSTALLS_RUN, busy, tgz, manifestOf, entryOf, servedBy, fixtureFetch, scratchDir, installRun, pyFiles and bytesOf, which the file declares below DA5.

DA9, the npm-package-arg oracle. Add `import { createRequire } from 'node:module'` beside it (the file already imports mid-file). npa = createRequire(NPM_CLI)('npm-package-arg') inside try/catch, null when absent; skip only then, with reason 'the host npm has no npm-package-arg'. accepted(spec): admit of lock({'': {name:'fixture', dependencies:{a: spec}}}) returns. registry(spec): npa.resolve('a', spec, '/ws').registry === true, or npa throws (a spec npm refuses installs nothing). Spread: 4000 specs from a seeded xorshift32 (state 0x9e3779b9; state ^= state << 13; state ^= state >>> 17; state ^= state << 5; return state >>> 0) over the alphabet "abvxX019.-_+*^~<>=| !'()tgzr/:@#%\\". Each spec has length next() % 12, with '.tgz' appended when next() % 16 === 0. Assert all three: every REGISTRY spec is accepted and no NON_REGISTRY spec is; no spec of REGISTRY + NON_REGISTRY + spread is accepted but not registry; and more than 1000 of the spread are accepted, so the oracle is not vacuous. No clock or Math.random input.

DA10, real npm: the positive control for the one bundled shape admission keeps. Options { skip: INSTALLS_RUN || NO_NPM, timeout: 180_000 }, and `if (busy(t)) return;` as in KI8. a = 'moe-fixture-a', whose tgz bundles e = 'moe-fixture-e': package/package.json {name:a, version:'1.0.0', dependencies:{[e]:'^1.0.0'}, bundleDependencies:[e]}, package/node_modules/<e>/package.json = manifestOf(e), and package/node_modules/<e>/bundled.txt = 'inside a\n'. Lock: '' = project {name:'moe-da10', version:'1.0.0', dependencies:{[a]:'1.0.0'}}; node_modules/<a> = entryOf(a, bundler, {dependencies:{[e]:'^1.0.0'}, bundleDependencies:[e]}); node_modules/<a>/node_modules/<e> = {version:'1.0.0', inBundle:true}. Build the tree with buildDependencyCache over fixtureFetch(servedBy({[a]: bundler})). Plant it, plus package.json and package-lock.json, through installRun exactly as KI8 does (toolchain JSON.stringify(dirname(dirname(process.execPath))), timeout 25). Assert [status, relays.length, tree.entries.length, the installed node_modules/<a>/node_modules/<e>/bundled.txt text] deep-equals [42, 1, 2, 'inside a\n'], with stderr as the message.

Then run the five new rows on the landed admission. DA6, DA8 and DA9 must fail (RED); DA7 and DA10 must pass. The prototype showed exactly that. Record it in the step note. No production code in steps 1-2.

comments.author: worker-3a9b4568
comments.content: Filer's note for the planner (worker-3a9b4568). A lead, unverified: npm ci also builds every non-root node's edges from its lock entry's own `dependencies`. A same-version `file:` spec there, e.g. node_modules/a {dependencies: {b: 'file:../../stub/b-1.0.0.tgz'}}, may replace a locked node the same way, if host admission doesn't check entries' dependency specs. Treat the class as "lockfile fields npm ci trusts that admission skips", not just the two verified routes. The other fix is making package-lock.json a protected path whose approved blob the guest checks. The scratch KIR harness in the description is the quickest place to try it.

Rejected: (a) duplicating the rules in the guest preflight (Python). That is two implementations of one rule; the guest installs exactly the bytes admission read; and it would change supervisorSha256 and join the guest-supervisor.py chain a80f46db -> 42e9990c -> a4a729dd -> 97341ad5. (b) The filer's alternative, a protected package-lock.json. Every legit dependency update would then need a lockfile approval, and it changes the protected-check contract. (c) Verifying node_modules/.package-lock.json after the install: the bytes are already installed, and 5ed445ca's plan rules out post-install-only detection. (d) Requiring resolved+sha512 on bundled entries and fetching them: real bundled entries carry neither (215/215 in a real npm@10.9.2 + fsevents@1.2.13 lockfile), so it would refuse every legit bundle. (e) A file:/git: prefix blacklist instead of a registry whitelist: npa also reads bare tarball names, leading-dot names, slashes and drive letters as local paths; the whitelist is checked against npa itself (DA9). (f) Refusing truthy link flags: not needed (see risks), so it stays minimal.
